questions.problem:
Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=\pi $ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{2}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,\sqrt{3}⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature: 

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=\pi $:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{3})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨-(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\cdot \frac{1}{2}),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\cdot \frac{1}{2},\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,0⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\pi ) & =\text{ }\frac{1}{4}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\pi ) & =‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖=\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\cdot \frac{1}{3},\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\cdot \frac{1}{3}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}),\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\pi ) & =\frac{1}{3}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}),\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,-\frac{1}{2}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨\sqrt{3},\,-1⟩\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=\frac{1}{4}$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

 

$$
T(s)=-\sqrt{1-2s}\,i+\sqrt{2s}\,j.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=\frac{1}{4}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\sqrt{1-2s})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{2s})\,j \\  & =-\frac{-2}{2\sqrt{1-2s}}\,i+\frac{2}{2\sqrt{2s}}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-2s}}\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2s}}\,j \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{1}{4}) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-2(\frac{1}{4})}}\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2(\frac{1}{4})}}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}}}\,i+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}}}\,j \\  & =\sqrt{2}\,i+\sqrt{2}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\frac{1}{4}) & =‖{T}^{′}(\frac{1}{4})‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{(\sqrt{2})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{2})}^{2}} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=5\pi $, if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

 

$$
T(s)=\frac{4}{5}\,i-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})\,j+\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})\,k.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=5\pi $: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4}{5})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3s}{5}))\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3s}{5}))\,k \\  & =(0)\,i-\frac{9}{25}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})\,j-\frac{9}{25}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})\,k \\ {T}^{′}(5\pi ) & =-\frac{9}{25}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\cdot (5\pi )}{5})\,j-\frac{9}{25}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\cdot (5\pi )}{5})\,k \\  & =-\frac{9}{25}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\pi )\,j-\frac{9}{25}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\pi )\,k \\  & =-\frac{9}{25}\cdot (-1)\,j-\frac{9}{25}\cdot (0)\,k \\  & =\frac{9}{25}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(5\pi ) & =‖{T}^{′}(5\pi )‖ \\  & =\frac{9}{25}\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{9}{25}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=1$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{s}^{2}}}⟨1,s⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature: 

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{s}^{2}}}⟨1,s⟩) \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{s}^{2}}}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{s}{\sqrt{1+{s}^{2}}})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{s}{(1+{s}^{2})^{3/2}},\,\frac{1}{(1+{s}^{2})^{3/2}}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{(1+{s}^{2})^{3/2}}⟨-s,1⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{(1+{1}^{2})^{3/2}}⟨-1,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}⟨-1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(1) & =‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}‖⟨-1,1⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=\frac{1}{3}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡3s,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡3s⟩,\,0\le s\le \frac{2\pi }{3}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{3}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡3s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡3s)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3s,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡3s⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡3s,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡3s⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡3s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡3s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-3\operatorname{cos}⁡3s,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3s⟩ \\  & =-3⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡3s,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡3s⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =|-3|\cdot \sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡3s+{sin}^{2}⁡3s} \\  & =3\cdot 1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{5}s}{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,0⟩\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨s-2\operatorname{arctan}⁡s,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡({s}^{2}+1)⟩,\,s\ge 0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(s-2\operatorname{arctan}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({s}^{2}+1))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{{s}^{2}-1}{{s}^{2}+1},\,\frac{2s}{{s}^{2}+1}⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{{s}^{2}-1}{{s}^{2}+1}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{2s}{{s}^{2}+1})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{4s}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}},\,\frac{2(1-{s}^{2})}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}⟨4s,\,2(1-{s}^{2})⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{(4s)^{2}+{(2(1-{s}^{2}))}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{16{s}^{2}+4{s}^{4}-8{s}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{4{s}^{4}+8{s}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{4({s}^{2}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2({s}^{2}+1)}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{{s}^{2}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s,$ where

$$
r(s)=⟨\frac{1}{3}(1-2s)^{3/2},\,\frac{1}{3}(2s)^{3/2}⟩,\,0<s<\frac{1}{2}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{1}{3}(1-2s)^{3/2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{1}{3}(2s)^{3/2})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot (1-2s)^{1/2}\cdot (-2),\,\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot (2s)^{1/2}\cdot 2⟩ \\  & =⟨-(1-2s)^{1/2},\,(2s)^{1/2}⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-(1-2s)^{1/2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}((2s)^{1/2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{2}\cdot (1-2s)^{-1/2}\cdot (-2),\,\frac{1}{2}(2s)^{-1/2}\cdot 2⟩ \\  & =⟨(1-2s)^{-1/2},\,(2s)^{-1/2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

  

Finally, the curvature is  

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{((1-2s)^{-1/2})}^{2}+{((2s)^{-1/2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(1-2s)^{-1}+(2s)^{-1}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{1-2s}+\frac{1}{2s}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2s(1-2s)}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=⟨1,\,t⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=⟨-\frac{t}{(1+{t}^{2})^{3/2}},\,\frac{1}{(1+{t}^{2})^{3/2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{t}{(1+{t}^{2})^{3/2}})}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{(1+{t}^{2})^{3/2}})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{t}^{2}}{(1+{t}^{2})^{3}}+\frac{1}{(1+{t}^{2})^{3}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{(1+{t}^{2})^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{(1+{t}^{2})} \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+{t}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{(1+{t}^{2})}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{(1+{t}^{2})^{3/2}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i+2\,j-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,k,\,{T}^{′}(t)=-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2({cos}^{2}⁡2t+{sin}^{2}⁡2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{2} \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡2t+{cos}^{2}⁡2t)+4} \\  & =\sqrt{4\cdot 2} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{(-\frac{t}{\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+\frac{{t}^{2}}{4-{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{4-{t}^{2}+{t}^{2}}{4-{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}} \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{t}{2\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{t}^{2}}{4(4-{t}^{2})}+\frac{1}{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{t}^{2}+4-{t}^{2}}{4(4-{t}^{2})}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}})}{(\frac{2}{\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}})}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Curvature Given a General Parametrization
questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\sqrt{3}\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,k,\,{T}^{′}(t)=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{2}\,i-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{2})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(\frac{-\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{1}{2} \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(\sqrt{3})^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+3} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is 

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{2}=\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Curvature Given a General Parametrization
questions.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point $t>0$ on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=⟨2t,\,-3{t}^{2}⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=-\frac{6}{(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}⟨3t,\,2⟩,\,t\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{6}{(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}\cdot \sqrt{{(3t)}^{2}+{(2)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6}{(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}\cdot \sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{6}{9{t}^{2}+4} \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(2t)}^{2}+{(-3{t}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+9{t}^{4}} \\  & =t\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{6}{9{t}^{2}+4})}{t\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}} \\  & =\frac{6}{t(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Curvature Given the Arc Length Parametrization And the Unit Tangent
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the curve $\mathbf r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

$$
\mathbf T(s) = -\dfrac{4}{5}\sin{s}\,\mathbf i+\dfrac{3}{5} \sin{s}\, \mathbf j + \cos{s}\,\mathbf k.
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Since we are given that $\mathbf{r}(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $\mathbf T(s)$ are both parametrized by the arc length $s,$ we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
\kappa(s) = \| \mathbf T'(s) \|
$$

Now, we differentiate $\mathbf T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡s)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡s)j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡s)k \\  & =-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡s\,i+\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡s\,j-\operatorname{sin}⁡s\,k \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\,i+\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\,j-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\,k \\  & =0\,i+0\,j-k \\  & =-k\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the curvature at the point where $s=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖=‖-k‖=\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}=1\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Curvature Given the Arc Length Parametrization
canonical_examples.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $\mathbf r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
\mathbf r(s) = \left\langle \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cos s , \: -\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cos s, \: \sin s \right\rangle,
\quad 0\leq s \lt 2\pi.
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let $\mathbf T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $\mathbf{r}(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s,$ we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
\kappa(s) = \| \mathbf T'(s) \| = \| \mathbf{r}''(s) \|
$$

Now, we calculate $\mathbf r'(s)$ and $\mathbf r''(s)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡s⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡s⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is 

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s)}^{2}+{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s)}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡s)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}{cos}^{2}⁡s+\frac{1}{2}{cos}^{2}⁡s+{sin}^{2}⁡s} \\  & =\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡s+{sin}^{2}⁡s} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Curvature Given a General Parametrization
canonical_examples.problem: Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $\mathbf r(t) = \left\langle 2\sin t, \:2\cos t \right\rangle.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let $\mathbf T(t)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter $t.$ Since we are given the curve $\mathbf{r}(t)$ parametrized by the parameter $t$ (not the arc length $s$), we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
\mathbf \kappa(t) = \dfrac{\left\| \mathbf T'(t) \right\|}{\| \mathbf r'(t) \|}
$$

First, we calculate $\mathbf r'(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the corresponding unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate $\mathbf T'(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
